title: Sonny and the Gentle Stream | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka follows a soft trickling stream through the bush at night, where the water hums over smooth pebbles like a tiny lullaby just for her. A calming bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Something was singing.

Little Sonny the quokka lifted her nose and listened.

It was not a bird. It was not the wind. It was something else — something low and soft and musical, just around the bend in the bush.

She followed it.

And there it was. A little stream, trickling over smooth round pebbles, its voice a gentle gurgle and hum. The water was shallow and clear and silver in the moonlight.

Sunny knelt at the edge and watched it move.

The water came from somewhere and went somewhere, easy and unhurried. It had no idea it was singing. It simply flowed, and the pebbles made the music for it.

Clink. Hush. Murmur. Bubble.

Each stone had its own small sound.

Sunny reached out one soft paw and trailed her fingers in the water. It was cold and clear and alive.

She pulled her paw back and sat with it curled against her warm tummy.

The stream kept singing.

Here was the thing about the stream, Sunny thought. It never stopped. Not for the dark. Not for the quiet. Not for any reason at all. It just kept going, one little gurgle at a time.

She found a smooth dry stone beside the water and sat upon it. The stone was cool beneath her and the air smelled of wet earth and green things.

Above her, the moon watched from behind a thin veil of cloud. A moth drifted past.

The stream sang on.

Clink. Hush. Murmur. Bubble.

Sunny's eyes closed, just for a moment.

Then for a little longer.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little stream. Goodnight, little one.
